children: Sustained tightness in the global diesel market is expected to benefit Indian refiners, particularly standalone refiners such as Reliance Industries (RIL).
Equirus Research in its latest commentary noted that tightening global diesel inventories could support refining margins even if crude oil prices moderate.
The Brokerage said that China’s diesel exports are expected to decline below 0.8 million tonne (mt) in November 2026, compared with 1.33 mt in August and 1.8 mt in September.
Commercial diesel inventories in China declined to 11.1 mt at the end of October, their lowest level since records began in 2011, it added.
The reduction in Chinese exports, alongside lower inventories in the US and other markets, could intensify competition for available diesel supplies and support refining cracks.
Equirus observed that strong diesel cracks have already supported refining profitability and believes sustained tightness would favour standalone refiners such as RIL.

For the week ended November 13, gasoil crack rose 0.9 per cent W-o-W to $61.4 per barrel, a decline of 14.4 per cent over the last three months. However, the cracks were higher by more than 24 per cent on an annual basis.

Jet Kerosene cracks rose 0.8 per cent W-o-W to $61.6 per barrel, up almost 20 per cent Y-o-Y.19.9 per cent Naphtha cracks improved to $2.4 a barrel from $-0.9 W-o-W and Fuel Oil crack stood at $-5.1 a barrel from $-5.2 during the same period.

As a result, oil marketing companies (OMCs) marketing margins performed better. Petrol margins eased to ₹6.3 per litre for the week ending November 13 from ₹6.5 a week before. Diesel losses narrowed to ₹21.5 per litre from ₹21.8.
Brent rose 1.5 per cent W-o-W to $95.8 per barrel. Indian Crude Basket fell 1.5 per cent W-o-W to $91.2 per barrel. Dubai rose by 0.9 per W-o-W and Oman was up by 0.6 per cent W-o-W.

Indian Rupee against the US dollar rose by 0.3 per cent W-o-W to 94.2 for the week ended November 13 a decline of 1.1 per cent and 1.2 per cent over the last three months and six months, respectively. However, it was higher by 0.8 per cent on an annual basis.

The International Energy Agency (IEA) in its oil market report for November 2026 said that the severe tightness in product supply, especially for diesel, remains the overriding concern of the broader market and consumers for now.

“Persistent attacks on Russian energy infrastructure continue to choke off the country’s diesel supplies to international markets, adding to losses from the Middle East. At the same time, Atlantic Basin refineries, particularly in the United States, are running hard to capture high margins, while improved crude availability in Asia and fresh Chinese product export quotas could support higher refinery throughput rates in the region,” it added

Notably, the accelerated release of IEA emergency diesel stocks over the coming months will provide a critical bridge across the supply gap until the global refinery system and product output recover.

title: Tightening global diesel inventories to support Indian refining margins
